column.title: Nothing juts out past the paragraph above it.
column.body: Text, tables, Dataview output and embeds share the same edges, up to 75rem, and less on a narrower pane. Live Preview and reading view look the same, so switching between them moves nothing.

palette.title:
Snow Storm by day.
Polar Night after dark.
palette.body: Light mode puts every background on nord6a, a Snow Storm step halfway between nord6 and white, and separates areas with nord4 hairlines. Dark mode is Polar Night. Accents come from Frost, states from Aurora, and where a Nord colour is too light for small text, the text takes a darker step of the same hue.

light.name: Light
light.note: Text steps on nord6a, raw Nord → Nord Lane: links 3.8 → 5.2:1, green 1.9 → 5.8:1, amber 1.5 → 6.1:1, red 3.8 → 5.6:1, violet 2.6 → 4.9:1.

dark.name: Dark
dark.note: Body text 9.2:1 on nord0, muted 5.7:1. Accents in nord8, the brightest Frost, so links and buttons stay clear.

tables.title: One table style, wherever the table comes from.
tables.body: Markdown tables, Dataview tables and the Live Preview table editor share one look: 15 px text, quiet uppercase headers, hairline rows and tabular numbers. In a pane under 700 px, tables drop to 14 px, and wide ones keep a readable width and scroll sideways.
tables.alt: A reading list table in a note, in Nord Lane's light mode
points: Headers in 11 px uppercase over hairline rows. On a long table they stay in view while you scroll.
Tags sit in the table as quiet pills, and numbers use tabular figures that line up on the right.
Dataview tables take the same style, and Dataview's - placeholders show as a faint dash.
cssclasses: [table-mono] sets one note's tables in Geist Mono, for ledgers.

cards.title: Cover cards for every collection.
cards.body: Optional gc-* classes turn a dataviewjs view into a grid of cover cards: books at 2:3, games in a square box, with corner badges, filter chips and a meta line under each title. A book without a cover file gets a typeset stand-in, as here.

specs.value: gc-grid, 160 px columns, 132 px for books

cards.alt: Four books as cover cards with typeset covers

dashboards.title: Dashboards in the same style as your notes.
dashboards.body: nl-* classes give your dataviewjs views a page head, stat strips, pills, tables, heatmaps and timelines, in the same type and colours as your notes. They do nothing until a view uses them.
dashboards.docs: The markup each one expects is in docs/components.md.
dashboards.alt: A reading dashboard built from the nl-* classes, in dark mode

mobile.title: The same notes on your phone.
mobile.body: Geist and Geist Mono are embedded with Latin and Cyrillic, Russian and Serbian alike, so phones and tablets render exactly what the desktop does. Layouts follow the note pane, not the screen: under 700 px, tables drop to 14 px and scroll sideways, stat strips fold to two across, and every tap target is 44 px.

options.title: Options when you want them.
options.body: There is no settings screen to learn. Add a class to a note's frontmatter when one note needs more room, a reading measure or a ledger. Change the column, the table text or the frontmatter size for the whole vault with Style Settings or a CSS snippet.
options.snippet: In a CSS snippet, for the whole vault
options.mono: this note's tables in Geist Mono
options.prose: reading text to a comfortable measure
options.bleed: tables and Dataview past the text, 0 by default

install.title: Two files, one folder.
install.body: Until Nord Lane is in the community theme browser, install it by hand. It works on desktop and mobile, with no plugins required.

steps.title: Copy
steps.text: Put both files in a folder named Nord Lane, inside your vault's themes folder.

steps.title: Choose
steps.text: Open Settings, then Appearance, and pick Nord Lane under Themes.

install.tested: Tested in Obsidian 1.15 on desktop and in its mobile emulation, in Live Preview and reading view, light and dark.

field.intro: Nord Lane is a calm, wide theme on the [Nord](https://www.nordtheme.com) palette. Light mode sits on **nord6a**, a step lighter than Snow Storm, and dark mode on Polar Night. Text, tables and embeds share one column, so nothing juts out past the paragraph above it.
